news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup: “I See Flamingos in the Final” – Abiola Backs Nigeria Against Venezuela, Hails SSA Adeboye’s Fatherly Support
news.lede: Eniola Abiola Atanda, Principal Assistant to the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Grassroots Sports Development, has tipped Nigeria’s Flamingos to reach the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, expressing confidence ahead of their quarter-final clash against Venezuela, Sports247.ng reports. Atanda, who watched Nigeria’s thrilling 2-1 victory over Mexico from the stands in Morocco, believes the youngsters possess the unity, determination and fighting spirit required to challenge for the trophy. news.title: FIFA Team to Visit Morocco for Inspection of Ongoing World Cup Preparations
news.lede: A FIFA team will conduct an inspection tour of the 2030 World Cup co-host countries, including Morocco, in November and December. A communiqué from FIFA said the delegation will meet with representatives of local, regional, and national authorities in the three countries and inspect candidate stadiums as part of the ongoing planning process. The FIFA delegation will visit several host cities in Morocco, including Agadir, Fez, Marrakech, Rabat, and Tangier, as well as Casablanca. It will also visit host cities in Spain, including Bilbao, Barcelona, Las Palmas, Seville, Zaragoza, and San Sebastián.

news.title: Pinoys sustain form, rip Macau
news.lede: DT·30 October 2026 · 1:28 AM PHT·2 MIN READ. NATHAN Caligdong connects a goal that lifted the Filipinos to a 2-0 win over Macdau in the preliminaries of the FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan. BAKU, Azerbaijan — The Philippine U15 Men’s National Football Team (PMNFT U15) notched their third straight win in the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival, beating Macau, 2-0, to start the classification stage Tier D round of 32 at the Hovsan Competition Complex. The young Filipinos dominated offensively, dominating possession and mounting numerous attacks to the Macau goal.

news.title: A European giant enters the race to host the 2038 World Cup
news.lede: France are weighing up a joint bid to host the 2038 World Cup, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo has confirmed.Diallo set out his country's intentions in an interview with the newspaper Ouest-France, with his comments published by the Tribuna website . France have not staged the men's World Cup since 1998. With the tournament now expanded to 48 teams, talk of a joint bid alongside Germany is gathering pace." I would say that our relations with the German Football Association are excellent, and that this would be a wonderful symbol of bringing a new spirit to European national-team football, and indeed to the whole continent as well," Diallo said.He also hinted that a third European nation could join the party."

news.title: U17 Women’s World Cup: Morocco puts its infrastructure at the service of African and world football
news.lede: The FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup, being held in Morocco from 17 October to 7 November, stands out not only for the historic run of African teams. It also highlights the quality of Morocco’s infrastructure and the Kingdom’s ability to host major international competitions. At the heart of the set-up, the Mohammed VI Complex brings together high-level pitches, on-site accommodation, catering, physical preparation and sports medicine. It gives the 24 participating teams training and match conditions that meet the most demanding standards, within a centralised format that also allows fans to watch several matches on the same day.

news.title: Morocco U-15 Exit World Cup After Paraguay Defeat
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s U-15 national team has been eliminated from the U-15 World Cup after losing 1-0 to Paraguay in the round of 16 on Wednesday. The match took place at the Hovsan Complex in Baku, Azerbaijan, where Paraguay secured a narrow victory to advance to the next round, ending Morocco’s campaign in the competition. The young Atlas Cubs were unable to overcome their South American opponents, who secured qualification with a single goal. Morocco had hoped to continue their run in the tournament but fell short in the knockout stage.
